name: Toshali Ratnagiri Resort Restaurant
area: Ratnagiri, opposite the ASI Buddhist site and museum
signature_dish: Odia and multi-cuisine meals near the Ratnagiri monastery
why_it_matters: The Diamond Triangle's three ASI Buddhist sites — Ratnagiri, Lalitgiri and Udayagiri — are rural and have almost no eateries, so the standout recommendation across travel guides is to time lunch at Ratnagiri. The Toshali Ratnagiri resort restaurant sits directly across from the Ratnagiri monastery gates and ASI museum, making it the single most practical sit-down meal on the whole circuit.
insider_tip: Plan your Diamond Triangle route so you reach Ratnagiri around lunchtime and eat here — Lalitgiri and Udayagiri have only packed-food options. Travel guides repeatedly advise carrying biscuits and water for the other two sites. Call ahead if visiting in a group, as this is a resort kitchen, not a high-turnover restaurant.
signature_address: Toshali Ratnagiri Resort, opposite Ratnagiri Buddhist Monastery, Ratnagiri, Jajpur District, Odisha 754295

name: Toshali Pushpagiri Resort Restaurant
area: Jajpur, on the Buddhist circuit road
signature_dish: Multi-cuisine meals on the Diamond Triangle circuit
why_it_matters: The Toshali group is the only hotel chain to have built dedicated infrastructure on Odisha's Buddhist Diamond Triangle circuit, with Toshali Pushpagiri in Jajpur as its second property serving the Ratnagiri-Lalitgiri-Udayagiri belt. Its multi-cuisine restaurant gives travellers a second hotel-grade dining option on a circuit where standalone restaurants barely exist.
insider_tip: Useful as a fallback meal stop if you are basing in Jajpur rather than reaching Ratnagiri at lunchtime. As a resort restaurant, it is best for guests or pre-booked groups; walk-in service can be slow off-season. The Diamond Triangle is otherwise a carry-your-own-food circuit beyond Chandikhol.
signature_address: Toshali Pushpagiri Resort, Buddhist Circuit Road, Jajpur District, Odisha 755006

name: Barabati Restaurant (Cuttack base)
signature_dish: Indian and Chinese mains in the Diamond Triangle's base city
why_it_matters: Many travellers run the Diamond Triangle as a day trip from Cuttack, roughly 80km away, since the three ASI sites have no real restaurants of their own. Barabati Restaurant near Barabati Stadium is one of Cuttack's established mid-range eateries — Tripadvisor 4.0/5 across 45 reviews — and is a reliable meal point at the start or end of the circuit.
insider_tip: Honest note: this is a Cuttack city restaurant, not a Diamond Triangle eatery — it is the base-city option for visitors who breakfast or dine in Cuttack before or after the Buddhist sites. Eat a full meal here and carry snacks for the sites themselves. Cuttack is also the gateway for Lalitgiri, the nearest of the three to the city.
signature_address: Barabati Restaurant, near Barabati Stadium, Cuttack, Cuttack District, Odisha 753001
